comment: Dr. Williamson is fun and quirky, and cares a lot about his courses. The content and discussions are very interesting, but sometimes the lectures can feel lengthy. Feedback can feel vague, but I would still for sure take this class again,

Dr. Williamson is remarkably bright and incredibly knowledgeable. Although his teaching style (and strangely endearing disposition) can take some getting used to, his class is well-structured, thought-provoking, and challenging - not to the point of difficulty, but to the point of personal reflection. Grades reasonably and gives excellent feedback.

Dr. Williamson is a very intelligent professor. His classes are mostly lectures and there are a couple midterm in class papers you write by hand. Pretty fair grader, and the volunteering, mandatory for the class, at Overby Sheppard Elementary School, has been a highlight of my semester.

easily the best prof I have ever had, lots of reading and lectures but it's all interesting stuff. no exams, just three in class essays in which we can have one sheet of notes. also doesn't grade too harshly, overall an amazing prof.

TW is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He not only is intelligent, but his work in Justice is what makes this class so engaging. He is a great guy and his class is interesting. You have two in-class writes and one final. He is not a harsh grader for papers. Overall, such a great guy - take his class!!! You also do not have to do readings.
Dr. Williamson is super intelligent and the material of this class was so interesting to learn about. Participation is not mandatory, and he is not too difficult of a grader on papers.

His classes and the ideas he brought to them were legitimately life-changing, especially for a PLSC student. TW is as knowledgeable about the abstractions of political theory as he is about so many realities of public policy. If you believe you care about the world around you, and you engage in good faith w the course, you won't regret taking him.
Dr. Williamson is a really nice person and cares about his students. 4 papers total and a final exam with essays.
He is awesome! Participation isn't mandatory and there's no cold calling. You don't need to do the reading. 4 papers and no mid-term. He's funny and really nice.

I LOVE Dr. Williamson. I have taken multiple classes with him and will take more given the chance. He is one of those professors that want to see you succeed and wants you to get an A in the class. He is a little awkward sometimes, but he is the sweetest guy in the world if you listen and get to know him. PLUS he is SO SMART
Loved this special topics class, so engaging and genuinely interesting.

He is an amazing teacher. I recommend taking his class if you have the chance. It is a lot of reading but he talks about it in class and it is usually interesting. He is funny and genuinely cares about his students.

Very nice. There is a lot of readings, I'd suggest you do it all. He knows so many people here in RVA, so networking with him would be a great idea. Definitely spend time in his office hours. His teaching style is unique, so be prepared for that, but overall a really great professor.

Big fan of Dr. Williamson. Initially a little awkward in class/it didn't seem like he had a super clear plan for where we were going but he is very knowledgeable about the subject and incredibly kind. Go to his office hours! Gives good paper feedback and is not too harsh of a grader. Very willing to work with students and has lots of connections.

Dr. Williamson is fine. He is a nice guy who cares about his work, but the class is mainly him just talking at you about the readings that you may or may not have done. The additional service requirement is also very taxing in addition to the three 6 page papers and longer final paper. You don't need to do the reading, but you won't learn much.

I love Dr. Williamson! He is so passionate about his work and class is so interesting. I loved taking his course. Put effort into your papers and know most of the reading and it is a solid A. the final paper is long though.

The reading was interesting, and he was a decent grader, if he remembered to grade our papers. He was frequently late, forgot to give assignments, and lost some students' papers. The extra service hours would have been fine, had he not restricted the class's options. He's a very interesting and experienced professor, but very disorganized.

A great an interesting person, although not always the most natural when it comes to leading a class. Overall he is certainly good, and he is a great person to know and keep in contact with after you take his class. He has some really interesting life experiences too. Somewhat difficult grader, but not unreasonable.

Do not take the contemporary Richmond class. A lot of the material is boring and class consists of discussing the material. He is probably the most awkward professor I have met thus far. Takes random pauses in the middle of sentences, and questions students in rapid succession causing no one to want to participate. Grades papers harshly. I don't think anyone in class has gotten higher than a B+ yet. The class involved 3 hour field trips into the city that are pretty pointless. Don't take him.

Amazing man, I aspire to be more like him every day. It's a tough course, but I can not stress the amount of incredible information you will learn and how your perspective will change after this course. DEFINITELY go to Thad during office hours, or meet him at Boatwright! He's amazing to just talk to and is honestly concerned with his students.
Excellent professor. a ton of reading but if you actually do it then you will be fine in the class. Thad's one of my favorite teacher's at richmond and i highly recommend him.
heavy reading load but most of it is interesting. keeps people engaged during class. at first sight he looks like he belongs up in the mountains but he's a brilliant professor

I'm in love. Dr.Williamson is the most quirky man I have ever met and I loved every minute of it. He is very unassuming and humble even though he is clearly brilliant. Somewhat of an idealist but that has just made me more optimistic. Do the readings! They are hard but will enlighten you and you will bring so much more to class having read.

the typical absent-minded professor.. ridiculously brilliant, and very amusing: he always has chalk on his shirt/pants, wears unmatching socks, and once even wore two different shoes to class. But he's so helpful and really wants people to understand what he's talking about.
Awesome professor and one of the smartest men I have met.  Makes you work and struggle but in turn you learn so much.  He is willing to help with anything and is always inspiring.

excellent teacher. He really challenges his students to do critical thinking. There is a lot of reading (in justice and civil society) but most of it interesting and worth getting through. Class is discussion based and is usually very engaging. Williamson is a brilliant man and I loved taking this class from him.

Outstanding professor; excellent course. His door is open and he is in his office A LOT willing to talk with students about anything.  He will loan you extra books to read on any subject you have questions about or are interested in.  He is apparently incapable of keeping his shirt tucked in or wearing matching socks, but he's brilliant and funny.

Intelligent but sometimes has trouble conveying his ideas. Some of the best readings you'll have in any class in terms of breadth and variety.  Unlike a lot of professors, he isn't afraid to state his beliefs although he doesn't force them on others. Very discussion oriented. Notes are primarily lists. Class not worthwhile unless you read.

I love this professor! He assigns readings that are long and semi-difficult sometimes, but nothing that you shouldn't be able to handle as a Leadership Major/Minor. He is INCREDIBLY smart, really nice, great to talk to, and makes jokes during class. I'd recommend him because he knows his material, and is definitely willing to help students anytime!

VERY DIFFICULT PHILOSOPHICAL READINGS FIRST 1/2 OF SEMESTER.  EASY READS ABOUT SOCIAL ISSUES.  MANY PAGES PER NIGHT.  VERY SMART AND KNOWLEDGEABLE.  ENTERTAINING PROF AND CLASS.  DIFFICULT GRADER BUT GIVES GOOD FEEDBACK.  INTERESTING DISCUSSIONS.  FOUNDED THE "**** DETECTION FACTOR" TO KEEP STUDENTS THINKING CRITICALLY.  HARD WORK BUT WORTH IT.
